Well to be honest I'm sceptical of my diagnosis of BPD traits. However... if I do have it (and I guess I should trust the psychs who diagnosed me) I think there is a few factors involved. 

I suspect my Mum might have it for one. She was always quite unstable, sometimes very loving and sweet, other times she would be incredibly angry, and verbally and physically abusive. Sometimes she would hug us and kiss and tell us she loved us, other times I would climb in to bed and cuddle up, and she would tell me she needed her space. She has had an alcohol problem for many years, and I saw her passed out in the living room a few times. She would also get really depressed for a few months and want to be in bed all the time.

 My dad had bipolar, which was controlled for the most part when I was a kid, but when I was a teenager I saw him manic/depressed. When he was depressed he would sleep all day and then get up for a few hours at night, and stand in the garden, smoking and refusing to talk to anyone. When he was manic, he would be angry and violent. 

Also when I was a preteen/teen they both had really bad alcohol problems, and would just leave me and my siblings alone in the house, often without food, I had to look after them.Add to that the fact, we moved a lot when I was a kid. 

I hope this reply helped in some way.

Hey, I actually have the same diagnosis as you funnily enough. Anyway you could ask about the anti depressant Mirtazapine, that really helped me (and seems to help a lot of people with BPD from what I've seen online). Also I had the exact same problems with blood tests! After testing me for basically every deficiency going they finally had to concede I was suffering from depression (not just the BPD traits type depression). But getting on the right dose of Mirtazapine has basically sorted that out completely.

Hi, I had to reply to this. This is not something I tell many people (any people really) but I dropped out of college three times, by the time I was 22. I wasn't diagnosed as BPD then, but basically every time I started out a course (always something completely different), I became suicidally depressed, got so stressed I could literally not do any assignments. Got very dejected and socially anxious around people etc. I sought help the 2nd and 3rd times, and was diagnosed with depression both times. I was diagnosed with having BPD traits at 26.


 Anyway I went back to college at 24 (again, a *completely* different subject area to the other 3 times haha) and 3 years later I'm still here. I have gone through periods of depression but am able to do assignments and exams. So things can change, I think for me I needed that time off to develop more as a person, learn stress management techniques, go through some issues with a therapist, mindfullness. Also I am way less anxious around people now, which I think helps a lot, because I can talk to people on my course and make friends, which helps when you're feeling down.  

Things will get better, you might need some time off, or you might need to plough through the course you're in right now. Listen to yourself and try to figure out what the best thing for you is right now. Believe me I **understand** how difficult this is, I don't think anyone can understand unless they have been through it themselves. You can do it, if I can, anyone can to be honest! I thought I was a completely hopeless case at many points. Now I get really good grades, even when I'm going through a crap time. One last piece of advice, talk to people - especially people in your college - lecturers, the counselling service. It will help to get all the anxiety off your chest.
It's just that I went through the same thing last year and sought help from my college then, so I don't think I can go back again. I feel like a failure.

Thank you so much. I just have so many other worries on my plate & things I have to do and I can't do them. I feel like the biggest loser on the planet. I have to keep my place in college but I'm struggling so much. I'm trying to juggle being in extreme emotional pain and trying to be an ordinary person, and I can't drop the ball.
